hosting.//headers: ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. Firebase Hosting applies every matching entry and, for the same header key, the one defined LAST wins — the opposite of rewrites, where the first match wins. This block used to list /assets/** first and /** last, which meant the catch-all silently overrode it and every fingerprinted asset shipped as no-cache: a full re-download of the whole bundle on every visit. Broad first, specific last. Verify after any change with: curl -sI https://car-log-project.web.app/assets/<hashed>.js

headers.//: Default for everything the SPA rewrite serves as index.html. A stale copy would pin users to an old build, because it is what points at the current asset hashes.
Stated explicitly as well as via /**, so the intent survives a future edit to the catch-all.
LAST, so it beats the catch-all above. Vite fingerprints these filenames, so a changed file is a changed URL — safe to cache forever.
